clue.text: Put an oil-well in Welsh town — that's a bloomer

indicators.note: in tells us the oil-well phrase is placed inside the name of the Welsh town

parts.note: Mold is a market town in north-east Wales
a rig is the drilling structure over an oil-well

explanation.surface: Someone proposes sinking an oil-well in a Welsh town, and the narrator calls it a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake, but here it is something that blooms. Mold is a small town in north-east Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A marigold is a garden plant prized for its orange flowers, so it is literally something that blooms.

clue.text: Second in importance

explanation.surface: A pure double definition with no story.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief instant of time and also weight or consequence, as in a matter of great moment.

clue.text: In a word, a bridge contract

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'In a word, a bridge contract (6)', which matches the scan: 'contract' can define REDUCE, but no parse of 'In a word, a bridge' gives letters, so a word may be doing two jobs or the setter meant a bridge term not found
annotationWithheld.clue: In a word, a bridge contract

clue.text: State the right method to' start moving

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
taken as written
a way of doing something is a method

explanation.surface: An instruction to declare the correct technique before setting off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb meaning say, but it is an American state. 'to' is a link; the stray apostrophe after it is a printing mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A nautical idiom: a vessel gathers way when it begins to move through the water fast enough to steer.

clue.text: Heatedly anti-change at an advanced stage

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters of heatedly and anti together

explanation.surface: Someone opposes reform hotly, but only when matters have gone a long way.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram fodder is HEATEDLY plus ANTI, with 'change' attached to 'anti' by the hyphen as the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something happening when it is almost too late, near the close of proceedings.

clue.text: Permitted from 3rd of July to August

indicators.note: 3rd of says take the third letter of the word July

parts.note: august means awe-inspiring, which is the old sense of awful (full of awe)

explanation.surface: A summer period, from early July to August, during which something is allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'August' looks like the month but is the adjective meaning majestic; AWFUL once meant inspiring awe.
explanation.definitionFit: Something permitted is allowed by law, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Gripped by first signs of Armada, he was almost sunk

indicators.note: gripped by means the word was is held between the letters that follow
first signs of means take the opening letter of Armada and of he

explanation.surface: A sailor in the Armada says he was nearly sunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The A of Armada and H of he close round WAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A deck awash is flooded with water, the state of a ship close to going under.

clue.text: Say tut-tut about more advanced soap

indicators.note: about means the sounded exclamation goes round the other piece
say signals that we spell out how the exclamation sounds

parts.note: fie is an old exclamation of disapproval, like tut-tut
latter means later, further on in time

explanation.surface: Someone clucks disapprovingly about a soap opera with a later storyline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' means the exclamation is written as it sounds, in the old spelling. 'Soap' suggests TV drama or washing, but soft soap is slang for flattery.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft soap is a slang term for insincere praise used to win someone over.

clue.text: Part of Richmond is featured in story too

indicators.note: featured in means these pieces sit inside the word for a story

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
Kew is a district in the London borough of Richmond, home of Kew Gardens

explanation.surface: A London district appears in a tale as well.
explanation.walkthrough: Kew, home of the botanic gardens, is a district of south-west London in the borough of Richmond upon Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean also, in addition.

clue.text: Censor in 22 is deliberate

indicators.note: in means the censoring word is put inside the other piece

parts.note: the answer to 22 is a word that in rhyming slang (china plate) means mate
to edit is to censor or cut text

explanation.surface: A censor at work in a country thinks things over.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 is the answer at 22-down, which is Cockney rhyming slang for a friend (china plate).
explanation.definitionFit: To deliberate as a verb is to ponder carefully, to think deeply.

clue.text: American lawyer has to conceal material

parts.note: a DA is a district attorney, a US prosecutor
to mask is to hide or conceal

explanation.surface: A US attorney needs to cover up some evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a rich patterned woven fabric.

clue.text: Breathe deeply before walking on and performing without preparation

parts.note: a sigh is a long deep breath
treading means walking on something

explanation.surface: An actor takes a deep breath before going on stage and improvising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'walking on' suggests an actor's walk-on part; here it is simply treading.
explanation.definitionFit: Musicians who sight-read play a piece from the score at first sight without rehearsal.

clue.text: The sound of a drum — it comes from inside of a shell

indicators.note: the sound of means we write a word that sounds the same as the drum word

parts.note: a naker is an old word for a kettledrum

explanation.surface: A drumbeat seems to come from within a shell.
explanation.walkthrough: NAKER is an archaic name for a medieval kettledrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother-of-pearl, the iridescent lining inside many mollusc shells.

clue.text: Fare from Cork rises with irregularity

indicators.note: irregularity tells us the letters of rises with are put in a disordered arrangement

explanation.surface: A fare increase from Cork comes in fits and starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' looks like a ticket price, but it is food. Cork is a city in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional Irish dish of mutton, potatoes and onions, food associated with places like Cork.

clue.text: Fascinating woman to embark in ship where connections are made

indicators.note: in means these pieces are put inside the abbreviation for a ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a witch is a bewitching, captivating woman
to board is to go on to a ship or vehicle

explanation.surface: A captivating woman goes aboard a liner where people meet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'connections' suggests social contacts; here they are telephone calls joined by an operator.
explanation.definitionFit: Old telephone exchanges had operators plug in calls, so they are the place where calls are joined.

clue.text: Master in charge of faculty

parts.note: to be over something is to be in charge of it
a faculty is a power or ability, like the power of speech

explanation.surface: A university head in charge of a department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master' and 'faculty' set up a college scene; here 'Master' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To master an opponent is to subdue or defeat them.

clue.text: Plumper fish on the stand

indicators.note: on means the fish sits above the stand in this down entry

parts.note: the chub is a freshwater fish
a bier is a stand on which a coffin rests

explanation.surface: A fatter fish displayed on a stand.
explanation.definitionFit: Both comparatives describe someone rounder, more full-bodied.

clue.text: Coerce both sides into a radio broadcast

indicators.note: into means the sides go inside the other piece
broadcast means the letters of a radio are scattered into a new order

parts.note: L and R are left and right, both sides

explanation.surface: Someone forces both sides of a dispute onto a radio programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns A RADIO into RAIOAD, and L and R are inserted after RAI.
explanation.definitionFit: To railroad someone is to force them into acting hastily.

clue.text: They've heard a swimming blue

indicators.note: swimming means the letters of the phrase move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Some people have heard about a swimming event in blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' looks like a colour but is the mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue means sad, and heavy-hearted describes someone weighed down by sorrow.

clue.text: In iron container, meat is slightly burnt

indicators.note: container means the iron symbol holds the meat inside it

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
lamb is meat from a young sheep

explanation.surface: Meat in a cast-iron pan has caught a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'container' is the signal: the iron symbol holds the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cooking term for food doused in spirit and set alight, so lightly scorched.

clue.text: Attitude derived from one's earliest ancestors

indicators.note: derived from tells us the letters come from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A belief passed down from one's first forebears.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is a standpoint or position taken on an issue.

clue.text: Battledress

parts.note: read the one word as two, a Crimean War battle and an item of dress named after it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Battledress' is one word for army uniform but splits into a battle and a garment. Balaclava was an 1854 Crimean War battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A Crimean War battle site, and a knitted hood covering the head, a garment worn by soldiers there.

clue.text: Country having ideologists nowadays as leaders

definitions.text: Country having ideologists nowadays as leaders

indicators.note: leaders means take the opening letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A nation run today by ideologues.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials of the first five words spell the country, and the whole clue describes it as communist-led.
explanation.definitionFit: A communist-governed state in East Asia, whose rulers are party ideologues.

clue.text: One brought into conspiracy to act as a leader…

indicators.note: brought into means the single letter goes inside the plot word

parts.note: a plot is a conspiracy
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A newcomer is drawn into a scheme to take charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To guide or steer, the job of someone who leads a ship or aircraft.

clue.text: … mocking one man in charge

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Ron is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man in charge is mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying the opposite of what is meant, in a sardonic way.

clue.text: 23 broadcast to West Country

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
Oman is a country in the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A leader's speech is broadcast to the south-west of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West Country' is the south-west of England, but here it splits into W and a country. 23 refers to the answer at 23-across.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who flies aircraft is an aviator.

clue.text: Go over the ground again about dead policeman

indicators.note: about means the summary word goes round the abbreviation for dead

parts.note: to recap is to recapitulate, going over points again

explanation.surface: Investigators revisit the scene after a policeman's death.
explanation.walkthrough: A redcap is a British military policeman, named for the red cap cover.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a member of the Royal Military Police, who wear red caps.

clue.text: In time, giver could be hurt

indicators.note: In means the mixed-up letters go inside the word for time

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

indicators.note: could be signals that giver is rearranged

explanation.surface: Eventually, someone generous may be wounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In time' looks like 'eventually'; 'could be' rearranges the giver letters to GRIEV for the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrieve is to wrong or distress someone.
